subject: Arbitration triggers & injunction notice protocol — Redwood MSA redlines
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@acmecommerce.com>, Contracts <contracts@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA redlines — arbitration triggers & injunction notice protocol

Hi Anna / Acme contracts team,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. We've completed an internal redline pass (attached: redlines_v3.docx) and have two discrete asks on dispute-resolution flow that I'd like to align on before we go further:

1) Arbitration trigger carve: our legal team is comfortable with arbitration for typical claims, but we need a narrow carve that preserves court access for emergency injunctive relief relating to data protection, IP theft, and unpaid funds. We'd like a short clause that says: "party seeking provisional injunctive relief may seek such relief in any court of competent jurisdiction prior to or during arbitration." Can you confirm Acme is open to that precise wording or propose equivalent language?

2) Injunction notice & escrow notice protocol: to streamline escalation, we propose a two-step notice: (a) 24-hour pre-notice to Contracts@example.com + GC with a short description of the remedy sought; (b) immediate filing rights if the remedy is urgent. Also, for funds disputes that might trigger escrow/chargeback, we'd like an agreed notice template (attached: injunction-notice-template.pdf) and a 72-hour cure window for billing-related holds unless there is a demonstrable imminent risk.

Internal folks: Marissa/Karthik, please weigh in on SLO/ops impact for preserved court access and the 72-hour cure.

Anna — can you send a one-paragraph response to these two items so we can fold them into the next commercial review with sales? If agreeable, we can proceed to countersign logistics.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redlines_v3.docx, Word doc — 42KB)
(Attachment: injunction-notice-template.pdf, PDF — 18KB)

From: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@acmecommerce.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@acmecommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — arbitration triggers & injunction notice protocol

David — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Quick answers to your two asks:

1) Arbitration carve: Acme is generally protective of arbitration for efficiency, but we are open to a narrow provisional-relief carve that preserves court access for narrowly defined categories (data breach, IP infringement, and imminent theft of funds). We can accept the suggested sentence with a minor tweak to avoid duplicative "competent jurisdiction" language. Proposed language: "Notwithstanding the Parties' agreement to arbitrate, either Party may seek provisional injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm, limited to claims involving (a) alleged unauthorized access to Customer Data, (b) alleged theft or misappropriation of intellectual property, or (c) imminent diversion or misappropriation of funds."

2) Injunction notice & escrow: Acme will agree to a 24-hour pre-notice where feasible; however, if Acme believes immediate court action is necessary (e.g., live exfiltration), Acme reserves the right to proceed without delay. On the 72-hour cure for billing holds: Acme's billing team asks for flexibility — they propose a "reasonable" cure period for payment disputes tied to invoice type; in practice, they'd prefer 48–72 hours.

We'll circulate a tracked change version accepting your provisional-relief sentence and suggesting the minor edits on notice timing.

--
Anna Brooks
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Commerce
(Attachment: ACME_MSA_comments.docx, Word doc — 28KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — arbitration triggers & injunction notice protocol

David — quick ops perspective:

- Preserving court access for the three categories above is fine for the product and security teams; it gives us the legal cover to work with customers during an incident.
- For billing holds: 48 hours is aggressive for finance ties, but acceptable as long as Contracts routes notices to our billing@redwood.com alias and we get clear invoice references. Please ensure the notice template includes invoice id, outstanding amount, and a primary contact.
- Ticketing/escrow: if Acme indicates "imminent risk" and files in court, we need a war-room contact and an agreed escalation list so SRE can prioritize KV cache dumps and log preservation.

I'll add those operational points into our next redline pass.

Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Brooks <anna.brooks@acmecommerce.com>, Contracts <contracts@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redlines — arbitration triggers & injunction notice protocol

Anna — thanks, that read is helpful and aligns with our internal ask.

Proposed next steps:
1) You to send a tracked change version of the MSA incorporating the provisional-relief carve language and the flexibility language on immediate filings for live incidents.
2) We'll update redlines_v3 with Marissa's operational checks (notice template fields + SRE war-room contact) and return a clean copy for countersign.
3) Sales will pause any signature until we have the matching escrow/notice template finalized.

I'll route the updated redline (v3.1) later today. If Acme agrees to 48–72 hour cure language for billing holds (with invoice specificity), we should be able to close commercial language next week.

Best,
David
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
